envelopes.rationale: Kinematic viscosity of real fluids: helium ~1.2e-4, air ~1.5e-5, water ~1e-6, mercury ~1.1e-7, heavy oils up to ~1e-4. Values above 1e-1 that the model 'remembers' from training are typically dimensionless slip-ups (e.g. cP confusion).
Ambient/reference pressure. 1 atm = 101325 Pa. Deep vacuum ~1e2 Pa, high-pressure industrial ~1e7-1e8 Pa. Below 1 Pa or above 10 GPa indicates a units error, not a fluid case.
Reference temperature. Cryogenic (LN2 ~77 K) to combustion (~2500 K). Values below 1 K or above 10^4 K are unit mistakes.
Prescribed inlet/wall speed magnitude. Microfluidics ~1e-3, civil/hydro ~1e0, high-speed gas ~1e2-1e3. Above 10 km/s or below 10 um/s is a units error for a continuum CFD case.
Boundary-condition pressure. Gauge pressures may legitimately be negative (suction) down to ~-1e6 Pa; absolute reference ~1e5 to 1e8 Pa. Extreme magnitudes betray scaled (bar/Mpa) inputs.
Domain extent per axis. Microchannel ~1e-4 m to large industrial ~1e2-1e3 m. Sub-micron or multi-kilometre domains are unrealistic for the OpenFOAM blockMesh box path.
blockMesh cell count per axis. Above 500 per axis quickly exceeds the memory a spike box can solve; reject values >2000 outright.
Surface/interface tension. Water-air ~0.072, mercury-air ~0.486, common fluids 1e-3..1 N/m. Values outside way of this are dimension slip-ups.
